author: Andrew Alpin
title: Why A Border Collie Should Never Be Your First Dog - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Alpin ,
1 hours ago
Picture this: You’re scrolling through social media and there it is – that mesmerizing video of a Border Collie weaving through agility courses like liquid lightning. Their intelligence shines through those intense eyes, their coat ripples with athletic grace, and you think, “That’s it. That’s my perfect first dog.” Yet what you’re seeing is the polished performance of a breed that demands nothing less than complete dedication from their human.
Border Collies can be challenging for first-time owners due to their high energy levels and intelligence. They do best with experienced owners who can dedicate time to training and exercise. The truth many discover too late is that this remarkable breed, while absolutely extraordinary, requires a level of commitment that can overwhelm even the most well-intentioned new dog owner.
Their Intelligence Can Work Against You Their Intelligence Can Work Against You (Image Credits: Pixabay) Border Collies are known for their extraordinary intelligence and are often cited as the smartest of all dog breeds. They are highly trainable but require mental stimulation and physical activity to be truly happy. This sounds wonderful until you realize what it actually means in daily life.
Sometimes their intelligence means they pick up on any loopholes in the rules, and use them to do what THEY want to do. Your brilliant Border Collie won’t just learn commands – they’ll analyze your consistency, test your boundaries, and exploit every weakness in your training approach.
A Border Collie will always seek to test boundaries. They will learn who is more of a pushover in the family and use that to their advantage, and they are smart enough to think a few steps ahead.
The Exercise Demands Are Overwhelming The Exercise Demands Are Overwhelming (Image Credits: Unsplash) They need at least 2-3 hours of vigorous exercise every day to fulfil their energy requirements. This isn’t a casual walk around the block – we’re talking about intensive, structured activity that challenges both their body and mind.
Your Collie will need a minimum of two hours exercise every day, but with Collies the more, the better! We’d recommend spreading this across the day in several walks with off-lead exercise in a secure area.
In all seriousness, Border Collies require an extensive amount of exercise, and a general rule of thumb is a tired Border Collie is a non-destructive and non-anxious Border Collie. If you can’t meet these demands consistently, you’re setting both yourself and your dog up for misery.
Mental Stimulation Is A Full-Time Job Mental Stimulation Is A Full-Time Job (Image Credits: Flickr) Without a job to do, they can easily become bored, leading to unwanted behaviours. Border Collies weren’t bred to be couch companions – they need constant mental challenges that go far beyond basic obedience training.
This intelligent breed loves a challenge, so keep them guessing with puzzle toys and plenty of mental stimulation. Border Collies are eager to please and will appreciate as much praise and attention as you can give them.
This intelligence, however, means they need regular mental stimulation. Without challenges to overcome and tasks to complete, a Border Collie can become bored and potentially destructive. Think puzzle toys, training sessions, agility work, and problem-solving games – every single day.
Separation Anxiety Destroys Homes Separation Anxiety Destroys Homes (Image Credits: Pixabay) They’re also prone to separation anxiety, so they don’t work well in homes where they’re left alone for the majority of the day. They need a lot of attention from their family. This isn’t just mild stress – it’s a genuine psychological condition that can devastate your living space.
Border Collies form strong bonds with their owners and may experience anxiety when left alone for extended periods. This can manifest as destructive behavior, vocalization, or attempts to escape.
If left alone for long periods, they may become anxious, leading to destructive behaviours like chewing or excessive barking. First-time owners often underestimate how completely a Border Collie can destroy furniture, walls, and personal belongings when anxiety takes hold.
The Herding Instinct Never Turns Off The Herding Instinct Never Turns Off (Image Credits: Wikimedia) Border Collies are generally good with families, including children and other pets, but their herding instincts may lead them to nip at heels or attempt to herd running children or animals. This isn’t occasional behavior – it’s a deep-seated drive that requires constant management.
They may also try to herd children or smaller pets as part of their instinctual drive. Picture your Border Collie nipping at your toddler’s ankles, chasing your cat, or trying to control every movement in your household.
Border Collies have strong herding instincts, which may manifest as chasing or nipping at children, other pets, or moving objects such as cars or bicycles. While this behavior is natural for Border Collies, it can be problematic in certain situations.
Health Issues Require Expert Navigation Health Issues Require Expert Navigation (Image Credits: Flickr) Border Collies can be more prone to epilepsy, a seizure disorder. This commonly starts around 1–5 years of age and will usually require anti-seizure medications to help control the condition. Managing complex health conditions requires veterinary knowledge and financial resources that overwhelm many first-time owners.
Hip dysplasia is an inherited condition where your dog’s hip joint doesn’t fit together. Dysplasia means bones rub on each other, leading to inflammation (swelling) and pain. The condition can cause arthritis over time.
Border Collies can also experience a genetic eye disease called Collie eye anomaly. Collie eye anomaly can cause malformations of the eyes, which can result in vision defects or blindness. These aren’t minor concerns – they’re serious conditions requiring ongoing veterinary care and potentially expensive treatments.
Training Demands Professional-Level Consistency Combined with their eager-to-please nature, training a Border Collie is fairly easy but their high energy and intelligence means they’re not the best choice for first time owners. Border Collies can be over-enthusiastic and are easily distracted so clarity, consistency and short training sessions are best to prevent both of you from getting frustrated.
Since border collies are so intelligent, they can easily be trained with experienced owners. If this is your first dog, you may want to visit a trainer to help you establish the basics with your dog.
However, Border Collies are so intelligent that training may be more difficult. It’s crucial, especially for a first-time owner, to research positive training techniques and consider investing in training classes. What seems like basic training to experienced owners becomes an advanced course for newcomers.
The Financial Reality Check The Financial Reality Check (Image Credits: Unsplash) Beyond the obvious costs of premium dog food and regular veterinary care, Border Collies require specialized equipment, extensive training resources, and potentially costly behavioral interventions. Finances are also an important factor to consider because some surgeries need to be performed by a veterinary orthopedic surgeon and are very expensive!
Emergency veterinary visits for injuries sustained during their intense exercise sessions, professional dog training to address behavioral issues, and the replacement of destroyed household items add up quickly. Many first-time owners find themselves financially strained trying to meet their Border Collie’s complex needs.
The reality is that cutting corners on a Border Collie’s care often leads to exponentially more expensive problems down the line. Their intelligence and energy levels mean that inadequate care doesn’t just result in a poorly behaved dog – it creates a destructive, anxious animal that requires professional intervention.
Your Lifestyle Must Revolve Around Them Your Lifestyle Must Revolve Around Them (Image Credits: Rawpixel) If you’re looking for a highly intelligent, energetic dog that thrives on activity and challenges, the Border Collie might be the perfect breed for you. They require an owner who is committed to providing them with the physical and mental stimulation they need to thrive. However, if you prefer a more laid-back companion or don’t have the time to commit to their exercise and training needs, another breed might be a better match for your lifestyle.
This breed doesn’t adapt to your schedule – you adapt to theirs. Weekend lie-ins become impossible when your Border Collie needs their morning run. Evening plans get cancelled because your dog requires training sessions. Vacations become complicated because finding adequate care for a Border Collie is challenging.
Do plenty of research before getting a Border Collie. Owning one takes a lot of time and commitment and you need to make sure you’re able to give them all the exercise and stimulation they need to stay happy and healthy.
Conclusion Conclusion (Image Credits: Unsplash) Border Collies are absolutely magnificent dogs – there’s no denying their exceptional intelligence, athletic ability, and loyal nature. However, they represent one of the most demanding breeds in existence, requiring a level of commitment that can overwhelm even dedicated dog lovers. Collies are loving and loyal dogs and you’ll get plenty in return for the time you spend with them.
The harsh reality is that many Border Collies end up in rescue centers not because they’re bad dogs, but because well-meaning first-time owners underestimated what they were taking on. If you’re truly committed to this breed, consider gaining experience with other dogs first, or better yet, volunteer with Border Collie rescue organizations to understand what you’re really signing up for.
Your first dog should be a companion that grows with you as you learn the ropes of dog ownership. A Border Collie will demand that you already know those ropes – and then some. What’s your honest assessment of your readiness for such an intense commitment? Think carefully, because both you and your future four-legged friend deserve nothing less than complete honesty about what lies ahead.

Your brilliant Border Collie won’t just learn commands – they’ll analyze your consistency, test your boundaries, and exploit every weakness in your training approach. Border Collies have strong herding instincts, which may manifest as chasing or nipping at children, other pets, or moving objects such as cars or bicycles.
